Subject: Billing alignment: May invoice KV-cache credits and rounding

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the runway call last week — overall the integration is going well. We just received the May invoice and there are a couple of line items that look off to us that I hoped you could clarify:

- The token usage shows a large number of "per-call" charges even though we rely heavily on the KV-prefix cache; we expected credits for re-used prefixes.
- The invoice rounding seems to have bumped our per-call units up by ~7% compared to our internal logging. It looks like an invoice-level rounding rule was applied, not per-session rounding, and that materially increased the billed tokens.

I'm attaching a redacted copy of the May invoice (nova_may_invoice_sample.pdf) and a short spreadsheet with our local token counts. Can you help explain how KV-cache credits are applied and what rounding rule you used? We need the details to reconcile before our finance team approves payment.

If this is a billing policy mismatch, we're open to a short pilot/credit to smooth things while we finalize packaging.

Appreciate a quick read — would prefer a short call if the rules are nuanced.

Thanks,
Maria Ortega
Head of Platform Integrations
Nova Labs

Subject: Re: Billing alignment: May invoice KV-cache credits and rounding

Hi Maria — thanks for the detail and the sample invoice. Short answer up front: we do apply KV-prefix credits, but the way credits and rounding interact can produce the discrepancies you're seeing — especially at high call counts with small per-call tokens.

Quick summary of the mechanics so you can reconcile with your spreadsheet:

- Token accounting: each API request is tokenized and billed per-token. For chat/generation requests we separate prompt + generation tokens.
- KV-cache credits: when a request hits the cache (prefix reuse), we apply a per-request credit equal to the prompt tokens attributed to the cached prefix up to the size of the prefix. We currently cap credits to avoid abuse; typical cap is 30% of prompt tokens per request for prefix reuse.
- Rounding/aggregation: billing is computed across the invoice period by aggregating billed tokens per request, then rounding to the billing quantum. Our current production quantum is 10,000-token increments for invoice aggregation and we apply a post-aggregation floor (minimum 5,000 tokens per distinct conversation window) which can push small sessions upward.

Why that can look worse: if your system generates many micro-requests that individually get KV-crediting but still fall under the conversation-floor, the floor can outsize the credit. Combined with 10k invoice quantum rounding, the invoice-level rounding can create a ~5-10% delta vs raw token sums.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) I'll propose a one-time retro credit for May equivalent to our estimate of net overcharge (we need to confirm with billing) — this would be an invoice credit rather than charge reversal.
2) Offer a 3-month pilot with clarified rules: we can run Nova under a pilot billing profile that:
   - applies KV-prefix credit with an increased cap (to 40%)
   - switches to per-conversation rounding at 1,000-token quantum for pilot traffic
   - provides monthly token accounting exports (CSV) for reconciliation
3) Pricing note: if Nova prefers a seat-bundle/commit model we can map the pilot usage into a committed SKU with a blended discount; we should discuss the size/term to land on a % discount.

I'm looping in Karthik and Kimberly for pricing/legal confirmation (see below). Happy to jump on a 30-min call — here's a few windows: Mon 6/14 10–11a PT or Tue 6/15 2–3p PT.

Best,

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 07:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: internal - KV crediting / rounding options for Nova Labs

Rachel / Kimberly — quick internal note on how I'd prefer we structure the pilot and the durable policy if we move forward. Keeping in mind fraud/abuse vector and accounting simplicity, recommended approach:

- Pilot rules (90 days):
  * KV-credit cap: 40% of prompt tokens per request (higher than prod to reduce reconciliation noise)
  * Rounding: switch to per-conversation quantum of 1,000 tokens for pilot traffic; invoice-level aggregation still applies but we round per-conversation first then sum
  * Reporting: daily per-conversation CSV export + a reconciled monthly summary with sample raw requests (anonymized)

- Durable policy (post-pilot):
  * Keep KV cap at 30% by default; allow account-level exceptions for high reuse workloads
  * Billing quantum: 10,000-token invoice quantum remains the default to keep invoices simple; exceptions require committed SKUs
  * Minimum conversation floor: 5,000 tokens remains, but for committed seat bundles we can waive the conversation floor when seat usage exceeds 25k tokens/day average

Pricing concession ideas (if they want durable credit):
- Map pilot usage into a committed 12-month bundle at a 15% discount on host-usage plus a 5% rebate for meeting a 2x prefix-reuse target (encourages engineering to leverage cache).

If you want to offer a one-time retro credit, cap it at 2 months of marginal overcharge. We should also get Finance to agree to a small reconciliation clause in the SOW so we don't reopen prior periods later.

Happy to join the call; if we offer discounts we should have a short MSA addendum and a mutual action plan.

Karthik
Head of Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference

Maria — thanks for the patience. Quick summary & proposed next steps to get this closed out:

Summary of what caused the delta
- KV credits were applied, but invoice-level aggregation + 10k quantum rounding + the 5k per-conversation floor increased billed tokens relative to your raw per-request logs.

What we're offering now
1) One-time credit for the May invoice: we'll issue a credit equal to the estimated net overcharge (billing will calculate and confirm amount by EOD Wed). This will be an invoice credit applied to your next invoice.
2) Pilot: 90-day pilot with the following profile: KV-credit cap 40%, per-conversation rounding at 1,000-token quantum, daily reconciliation CSVs.
3) If you convert to a committed bundle within the pilot: 12-month commit with 15% usage discount and terms to waive conversation-floor above an agreed usage threshold.

Next actions
- I'll have Billing compute the retro credit and send a short credit memo by Wednesday EOD.
- Can we do Mon 6/21 10:00–10:30a PT for a 30-min alignment call to lock pilot terms and agree the mutual action plan? Please confirm a time.
- I'll attach a short SOW addendum for the pilot that includes the pilot billing profile and reconciliation cadence (DocuSign link to follow).

Thanks again — we'll make this painless.

Best,
